sections.heading: Hajime Shoji admits League One lacked communication before eligibility U-turn
sections.body: In late August, Japan Rugby League One backtracked on player registration rules that would have classed some Japanese passport-holders born abroad as foreigners, limiting their domestic opportunities. After legal challenges and a fierce backlash from players, the league's exception now covers those who acquired Japanese citizenship by May 2025. Managing Executive Director Hajime Shoji admitted the league had lacked communication with affected players. The rules were due to take effect in the 2026-27 season, which begins in December.

sections.heading: Japan Rugby League One reverses foreign-born player rules after player backlash
sections.body: In late August, Japan Rugby League One backed down on rules that would have treated some Japanese passport holders born abroad as foreigners for domestic play, settling a court case brought by 24 players, Timothy Lafaele among them. Shoji conceded, "We lacked communication with players who would be adversely affected by the changes." The concession covers players who gained Japanese nationality before the end of May 2025, but the new system still reduces places for foreign-born players eligible to represent Japan.

lead.why: It is the most talked-about Japan story left in the pack, and its eligibility angle touches the national team's player pool.
